newsitem.title: GABON: Congo Brazzaville truce holds, no talks progress.
newsitem.headline: Congo Brazzaville truce holds, no talks progress.

text.p: Mediators once again failed to bring envoys of the Congo Republic's warring parties face-to-face in Gabon on Thursday but a truce held in the troubled oil-producing nation's capital Brazzaville.

The radio station run by former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso said in Brazzaville that the two sides had been studying proposals and fresh talks could take place on Friday. There was no comment from President Pascal Lissouba, Sassou's rival.

U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said on Wednesday that the two sides had been presented with a draft accord offering a range of options. He had anticipated talks in Gabon's capital Libreville on Thursday.

Sahnoun and Gabon's veteran president, Omar Bongo, who ended similar ethnic and political clashes that killed 2,000 people after a disputed 1993 parliamentary election, held separate talks with delegation heads on Wednesday.
Lissouba and Sassou remain in Brazzaville.

Sassou's radio there said on Wednesday that the sticking point was a decision by Congo's Constitutional Council to extend Lissouba's mandate until elections can be held. His mandate ends at the end of August.
The council cancelled a planned July 27 presidential election. Sassou did not object to that but wants a government of national salvation.
The showdown began on June 5 after the army surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias.
